newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine traders see gov't soy forecast slipping.
newsitem.headline: Argentine traders see gov't soy forecast slipping.

text.p: Argentine traders mainly thought Wednesday that the government was likely to further reduce its 1996/97 soybean production forecast.

The Agriculture Secretariat on May 21 cut its soybean crop forecast to 11.5 million tonnes from 12.9 million tonnes, but many in the market feel it has still not properly taken account of a long patch of dry weather in crop lands.
"They should cut it," said one trader, who said he thought output was 11.2 million tonnes.
A second trader said, "I think most of the market is working at between 10.5 million tonnes and 11 million tonnes."
Another trader said he thought the government was likely to cut its estimate, although he thought 11.5 million tonnes was not such a bad figure as some say.
"It's hard to say. It's still hard to work out how many beans there are from the crushing circuit figures," he said.
Some brokers have said they see output as low as 10.5 million tonnes.
The new forecast is due to be announced at 1600 local/1500 EDT. Argentine soybean harvesting is now almost completely over.
